`slicer ai relay` exists, but nothing points to it. `slicer --help` describes `ai` as "onboarding instructions for coding agents", and neither `ai instructions` nor `ai instructions --rest` names the relay. Name it in the top-level help and add a pointer to the guide part that `--rest` also prints.

**Not in this slice:** changing the relay text, changing `skill_text` or the installed SKILL.md copies, and new `ai` subcommands.

## Why

The owner looked at `slicer --help` and found no way to the relay. To find it, you have to guess that `ai` has subcommands and run `slicer ai --help`. Agents follow `ai instructions`, and agents that load the skill follow `ai instructions --rest`. Neither text mentions the relay, so an agent will not run a relay unless it is told the command name. s241 left the pointer out of scope on purpose. This slice adds it.

## Files

- `src/slicer/cli.py`: the `help=` of the `ai` subparser (line 2722 at filing).
- `src/slicer/ai.py`: a one-line pointer in a part that both `INSTRUCTIONS` and `rest_text()` include (`IMPLEMENT_MORE` or `HANDOFF_SECTION`), so the skill text does not change.
- `docs/commands.md` and `README.md` if they quote the `ai` help line. `CHANGELOG.md`.
- `tests/test_ai.py`.

## Implement

Reword the `ai` help so it names the three subcommands, for example "agent onboarding: instructions, skill, relay". Add one sentence that tells an agent to run `slicer ai relay` to run one slice through implementer, reviewer, architect and gate agents. Put it in a part that both the full guide and `--rest` print. Keep it neutral about the finish step: it must not name `done`, so the handoff-project rule (a handoff guide never tells an agent to run `done`) still holds. Update any test that pins the guide or help text exactly.
